results.reason: Issue 1 identifies MSA §3.2 nationwide exclusivity over all warehousing, freight and delivery services, contrasts it with TS §4.1 (last-mile, NYC metro only), and provides a redline narrowing exclusivity to last-mile delivery in the Service Area.

Issues 2 and 3 note that §11.3 carves out only Customer's §10.2 indemnity, leaving it uncapped, while Provider's §10.1 indemnity stays subject to the 12-month fee cap. The response explains the one-sided exposure and recommends making the carve-out apply to either Party's indemnities, which makes it mutual.

Issue 6 identifies Delaware law and Wilmington courts in DPA §9.1, the conflict with MSA §18.1 and TS §11, and that the DPA is first in precedence under MSA §2.3. It recommends conforming the DPA to MSA §18 (New York).
Issue 4 covers the 3-year auto-renewals and the 15-day window ending 120 days before expiry. It explains the lock-in cost and recommends 1-year renewals, a 60-day notice period and a reminder notice.

Issue 5 contrasts SOW §8.2 free Provider assignment with MSA §17.4 Customer-only restrictions. It notes the risk of transfer to an 'unknown, unrated or competitor-owned entity' and recommends a mutual consent clause ('Neither Party shall assign').
The memo states MSA §2.3 puts the DPA first, notes the MSA prevails over the SOW, and quotes the order 'DPA… then this Agreement, then the Statement of Work.'
Issue 3 quotes the cap as 'the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim' (MSA §11.1).
It is a memo addressed to the Supervising Partner, and each issue includes Where, Why it matters and a Recommendation.
Issues are titled 'in Order of Importance' with severity labels, and Part 4 lists items to raise with the client before the next turn.
The memo concludes the DPA overrides the MSA forum for data disputes and flags the inconsistency; it does not say New York controls or that the documents are consistent.
The memo expressly states the exclusivity clause exceeds the term sheet scope.
